newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq strength builds, hits third straight high.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq strength builds, hits third straight high.

text.p: Nasdaq shares rallied to a third consecutive record high on Tuesday, bolstered by continued strength in personal computer stocks, traders said.

The Nasdaq composite index gained 11.16 points, or 0.78 percent, to 1443.11, topping the previous record high of 1431.95 set on Monday. The session was slightly weighted towards declining issues, with losers beating gainers 2192 to 2105 on total volume of 622 million shares. The Nasdaq gains offset an 11.31 point drop in the Dow industrials, which closed unofficially at 7760.78.
"Some of the top-shelf techs have had a good couple of days. There's some messages out there that business is pretty strong," one trader said.

Shares of personal computer stocks continued a strong rally, driven by an optimistic outlook for the quarter and bullish comments by Merrill Lynch on industry bellwether Compaq Computer Corp, analysts said.

Dell Computer Corp also gained 5-1/2 to a new 52-week high of 120-7/8. Dell surged further after comments on Monday that it was "very pleased" with the second quarter and that momentum remained strong in Europe, traders said.
